headline: Climate crisis made Canada's wildfires twice as likely, study finds
summary: Nearly 700 fires are burning across Canada; World Weather Attribution says fossil-fuel heating made the conditions twice as likely.
script: A new study says the climate crisis made Canada's wildfire conditions twice as likely. Nearly seven hundred fires are burning, and scientists warn such fire weather is no longer rare, as towns face evacuation and smoke spreads across North America.
imageAlt: A wildfire burns along a hillside at night, reflected on a lake in British Columbia.
imageAltTwo: Smoke and flames rise through a coniferous forest in Canada.

sources.title: Human-driven climate crisis fuels Canada's deadly wildfires, study finds
